claims.claim: The per-project rollout of impersonation is blocked because the CI diff step fails when impersonation is enabled, as the diff runs as the destination service account and lacks permissions for cluster-scoped resources (as demonstrated in T-26271), leading to the decision to not enable impersonation per-project until the diff story is fixed (notes/note-1.md).

The reverse deletion strategy in progressive sync causes the ApplicationSet controller to wait for an application to be fully deleted before proceeding to the next, leading to an infinite loop when an application is stuck in the Progressing state (as seen in T-28511), blocking the deletion of subsequent applications.

Without a debounce, each push of hydrated manifests by the manifest hydrator to the git repository immediately triggers a new Argo CD sync operation, which when using progressive sync causes the ApplicationSet controller to restart the rolling sync wave from the beginning, potentially leading to repeated sync attempts and instability.
The hydrator's machine-generated commits to git lack GPG signatures, which causes rejection if the hydrated branch requires signed commits, breaking the hydrator's own sync mechanism.

The strategy.md commits to not implementing ordered deletion for ApplicationSet children (teardown remains manual), but the prd-progressive-sync-deletion.md proposes to implement ordered deletion for ApplicationSet via progressive sync.

The conflict between strategy.md's commitment to manual teardown of ApplicationSet children and the PRD's proposal for ordered deletion via progressive sync creates a risk of breach of contract necessitating review by a licensed professional.

Hydrator pilot repos cannot use progressive sync while using the hydrator until a debounce is implemented, because each hydrator push restarts the rolling sync wave, blocking the hydrator pilot work (T-27949) from using progressive sync.

Rolling out impersonation per-project (which requires flipping the flag on a project) is blocked until the diff story (T-26271) is fixed, as per the decision in note-1, blocking the impersonation feature rollout (rfc-001-sync-impersonation.md).
The hydrator rollback work (T-27327) is deprioritized to next quarter, as per the decision in note-1, blocking the work to implement history and rollback for the source hydrator.

RFC-001 commits the impersonation feature to be enabled/disabled only at the system level (fleet-wide) while note-1.md commits to rolling it out behind a per-project flag, creating a contradiction in the scope of the feature flag.

Strategy.md commits that ordered deletion of ApplicationSet children is out of scope for rollout orchestration (will not be implemented) while PRD-progressive-sync-deletion.md commits to implementing a Reverse deletion strategy that deletes applications in the reverse order of deployment, creating a contradiction about whether ordered deletion of ApplicationSet children is in scope.
The roadmap states serviceability is completed and includes more metrics, but there is an open ticket requesting metrics for progressive sync, indicating the metrics are not yet implemented.

Without metrics to measure the duration of each step in the progressive sync deletion strategy, we cannot detect when a step is delayed due to a stuck application, which could lead to an infinite loop going unnoticed as described in T-28511.

There is no metric to track the frequency of diff failures caused by insufficient permissions of the impersonated service account, which is needed to monitor the health of the impersonation feature when server-side diff is enabled.

The CI diff failures (T-26271) occur because with impersonation enabled, the diff runs as the destination service account which lacks patch permissions on cluster-scoped resources, as noted in notes/note-1.md, and the impersonation feature is enabled via rfc-001-sync-impersonation.md.

The stage-branch promoter being a shell script with no owner (notes/note-1.md) is addressed by the Manifest Hydrator feature (rfc-002-manifest-hydrator.md) which introduces a commit server for pushing hydrated commits.

The delete/recreate loop (T-28511) when using ApplicationSet with Progressive Sync and reverse deletion order occurs because the Reverse deletion strategy (prd-progressive-sync-deletion.md) waits for one application to be fully deleted before moving to the next, and a stuck application never completes deletion.

Each hydrator push (as described in rfc-002-manifest-hydrator.md) triggers a new sync in Argo CD, which for ApplicationSets using Progressive Sync (prd-progressive-sync-deletion.md) restarts the rolling sync wave, as noted in notes/note-2.md regarding the wave-restart thing on hydrated repos.

Server-Side Diff on external clusters ignores destinationServiceAccounts and runs as the cluster credential because the impersonation feature (rfc-001-sync-impersonation.md) is only implemented for sync operations, not for diff.

proposals.change: note the root cause on that ticket so the reporter stops chasing the cluster secret
proposals.citedLine: the CI diff failures (the missing-permissions one, T-26271) got root-caused on the call: with impersonation on, diff runs as the destination service account which doesn't hold patch on cluster-scoped stuff. someone should note the root cause on that ticket so the reporter stops chasing the cluster secret.
hydrator rollback work (the history & rollback ticket, T-27327) is deprioritized to next quarter. dev pair moves to the progressive sync deletion loop instead. ticket should say so.

proposals.change: hydrator pilot repos must not use progressive sync until there's a debounce
proposals.citedLine: the wave-restart thing on hydrated repos: we confirmed each hydrator push restarts the rolling sync wave. interim call from the review: hydrator pilot repos must not use progressive sync until there's a debounce. the pilot ticket (T-27949) should carry that restriction so the next team doesn't trip it.

deltas.body: we decided it goes behind a per-project flag, not fleet-wide. nobody flips it on a project until the diff story is fixed. that's a real decision, not a maybe.
deltas.citedLine: impersonation rollout: we decided it goes behind a per-project flag, not fleet-wide. nobody flips it on a project until the diff story is fixed. that's a real decision, not a maybe.

deltas.body: mitigation for now: incident runbook says switch the ApplicationSet to AllAtOnce deletion before deleting any child app by hand. that's the operational rule until the controller fix lands — worth remembering as a standing practice.
deltas.citedLine: the delete/recreate loop (T-28511) reproduced in staging with the reverse deletion order. mitigation for now: incident runbook says switch the ApplicationSet to AllAtOnce deletion before deleting any child app by hand. that's the operational rule until the controller fix lands — worth remembering as a standing practice.
